name: Consensus Decision-Making Protocols
region: Global (Haudenosaunee, Quaker, Anabaptist, East African, Polynesian)
summary: Decision-making systems requiring broad agreement through structured deliberation rather than simple majority rule, originating independently across multiple cultures.

claims.statement: Haudenosaunee consensus process directly influenced Quaker decision-making practices through colonial-era contact
Consensus protocols produce more durable agreements than majority-vote systems in community-scale governance
Multiple independent origins demonstrate convergent social evolution toward consensus under conditions of political equality

evidence.source: Jennings (1984) The Ambiguous Iroquois Empire, Norton
Sheeran (1983) Beyond Majority Rule: Voteless Decisions in the Religious Society of Friends
Susskind & Cruikshank (1987) Breaking the Impasse: Consensual Approaches to Resolving Public Disputes, Basic Books
East African village council archaeology, Connah (2001) African Civilizations
Polynesian fono (council) traditions documented by Mead (1969)

notes: Cross-links: unlocked by both haudenosaunee council (Great Law of Peace) and restorative justice; feeds into federalism templates. Demonstrates that governance innovations flow across cultural boundaries.
